video.title: Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft 9 cat Pick 3 | Shai Build

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team 9-category head-to-head mock draft from pick 3 and takes Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. He says he would take Luka Doncic at 3 about 75% of the time, but the gap is small. His main theme is that strict ranking order (ordinality) is a fallacy: drafting is about probabilities, and players a few spots apart are close in value. His roster: Shai, Alperen Sengun, Brandon Miller, Jaylen Brown, Keyonte George, Zach Edey, Day'Ron Sharpe, Caleb Wilson, Yaxel Lendeborg, Jalen Green, Miles Bridges, Grayson Allen, Paul Reed and Cam Johnson. Along the way he covers preseason news: the Warriors' expected starters, Ben Simmons possibly starting for the Kings, Leonard Miller's strong preseason in Chicago, and his worries about Josh Giddey and Reed Sheppard. He is happy with his team. He also says Kareem's mostly autodrafted team projected best, though many of its players come with high variability.

rules.text: Fantasy rankings are probabilities, not certainties. The value gap between players ranked close together is small, so picking slightly off the ranking order is fine.
rules.quote: None of it ever  works that way. It's all probabilities. It's all this might happen and this might be here.

rules.text: Do not treat ranking order as everything. Pick 13 is not really three slots better than pick 16.
rules.quote: we need  to remove the idea that ordinality is the be all and end all.

rules.text: In head-to-head leagues he sorts projections by head-to-head value. He looks at the next 12 players on that list instead of always taking the top one, because their value numbers are close.
rules.quote: I don't grab the top ranked player. I do sometimes, but I don't always. I look down at the next 12

rules.text: When choosing among close players, think about whether a player could come back to you next round and which categories (assists, scoring, percentages) you need and can still find later.
rules.quote: Hey, could this guy come back around? Am I really needing assists or do I  need some scoring?

rules.text: After the first two rounds, he only calls a pick a reach if he would take 10 to 15 players ahead of that player. A gap of about four players does not matter.
rules.quote: If there is 10 to 12 guys, 10 to  15 guys that I would prefer ahead of that player, that's when I'll say it.

rules.text: He flags a pick as early when the player goes about 30 spots ahead of where he ranks him.
rules.quote: when someone's 30 spots ahead of where I've got them,  that that is where I go.

rules.text: ADP ranges are very wide, so where a player actually goes varies a lot from draft to draft.
rules.quote: All of these picks have pretty large ranges.

rules.text: Every mock draft is different. One mock is not a blueprint for a draft slot.
rules.quote: this is not a blueprint of what I would do at pick three. It's what I'm currently doing  at pick three.

rules.text: Luka is his usual pick at 3 in head-to-head, but in roto he might take Shai over him.
rules.quote: I would take Lucer. If I'm in Roto, I might take Shay over him.

rules.text: Around round 10 it is time to take upside flyers.
rules.quote: cuz we are in round 10. It is flyer time.

rules.text: Being 'exciting' means a player has a path to beat his draft slot, not just being solid.
rules.quote: by excitement, I mean like have you got  something to be able to go past this number?

rules.text: Be careful with preseason standouts. Good preseason numbers may not hold once regular rotations and minutes are set.
rules.quote: good preseason numbers, but how does it how will it translate across during the regular season

rules.text: He will not draft players with a serious injury history, such as a partially torn Achilles, inside the top 120.
rules.quote: I'm not doing it inside the top 120 partially torn Achilles injury history not happening
